business_problem: Stryve's net sales fell ~41% to $17.7M in FY2023 while its own 10-K cites 'discontinuation of non-profitable accounts' - distribution grew to H-E-B, Walmart, Whole Foods and more, but the shelf is not turning browsers into buyers, and biltong is still an unfamiliar word to most Texas shoppers.

findings.finding: Content analysis of 1,400 public reviews (collected 2026-11-07): 29% mention taste/flavor unprompted, 20% mention repeat/bulk orders, complaints only 4%
findings.therefore: Demo Days and creator taste content lead - product experience converts; the gap is reaching new shoppers

findings.finding: 12% of 1,400 reviews mention health/clean-label benefits (sugar-free, high protein, keto) and 5% explicitly compare it to jerky or other meat snacks
findings.therefore: Position biltong as the premium upgrade to jerky - clean-label proof is the hook for performance and parent segments

findings.finding: Only 4% of 1,400 reviews mention discovering Stryve in a store; the review base is overwhelmingly DTC/repeat buyers
findings.therefore: Retail trial must be manufactured at the shelf (demos, education, coupons) because organic retail discovery is weak

findings.finding: 20% of 1,400 reviews mention repeat purchase or bulk orders - the strongest loyalty signal in the dataset
findings.therefore: Campaign ends with a repeat/bundle offer; the product already earns reorders when people try it

findings.finding: Audit (8 public sources, 2026-11-07): 10-K reports net sales $17.7M FY2023 vs $29.9M prior year (~-41%) while distribution spans H-E-B, Walmart, Whole Foods, Sprouts, CVS, Circle K, Love's
findings.therefore: This is a velocity problem, not a distribution problem - fund trial at the shelf in stores already carrying it

findings.finding: Biltong is a nascent category in Texas - H-E-B carries it in the jerky aisle store-by-store, and few shoppers know the word; competitors are fragmented regional brands
findings.therefore: Own the education moment: 'It's not jerky - it's biltong' becomes the memorable, ownable line

programs.name: Biltong 101 Demo Days
programs.mechanic: 12 weekend demo shifts at 6 DFW H-E-B test stores; 'What is biltong?' sample cups beside the jerky/meat-snack set; QR to the '$2 off 2 bags' coupon. 6 matched control stores get the coupon but no demos or clip strip, isolating the in-store effect.

programs.name: The Jerky Aisle Upgrade
programs.mechanic: Pitched to H-E-B's snack buyer in October-November: clip strip inside the meat-snack set at 6 test stores, shelf talker ('It's not jerky - it's biltong'), and '$2 off 2 bags' app coupon at DFW H-E-B stores carrying Braav. Fallback if declined: demos + brand's own printable coupon.

programs.name: Jerky or Biltong?
programs.mechanic: 3 DFW food/fitness creators run blind taste-offs: Braav biltong vs. the beef jerky they actually buy, with macros on screen. Link goes to a store finder + coupon, or the online starter pack with code BILTONG. #ad disclosure on every post.

programs.name: The Biltong Story
programs.mechanic: Plano HQ + South African heritage (Warren Pala) + ex-NFL founder (Gabe Carimi) in 3 short videos and 3 emails/SMS to the existing list, each ending with the store finder and starter pack code - converting the 20% repeat-buyer base into bulk/reorder buyers.

assumptions.text: Blended net revenue per purchase $18: 50% retail coupon purchases at ~$8 net (1-2 bags x ~$5 wholesale minus $2 coupon) + 50% online starter packs at ~$28 (4 bags at ~$9 with code discount); confirm wholesale price with company
Blended gross margin 45%: meat-snack COGS higher than plant jerky; 10-K margins historically 25-40% - confirm with company financials
H-E-B store-level baseline velocity unknown; measured week 0 via shelf audit + company sell-through data
Impressions 1.5M = ~1.0M paid at ~$5.5 CPM ($5,500) + ~500K creator views (3 creators); 1.5% click rate; 10% click-to-purchase (validate week 1). In-store exposure not counted
Stryve and H-E-B would approve in-store demos and a digital coupon (proposed, not confirmed)
DFW fitness/food micro-creators (10K-80K followers): ~$1,000 per video incl. product
In-store demo shift ~$250 (4-hr demo staff via sampling agency + product for ~300 samples)
$2 off 2 bags manufacturer coupon; its cost is netted out of revenue per purchase (A1), not a separate line
Production (shelf talkers, clip strips, sample cups, design) ~$900 via local print shop quotes
Email/SMS + landing page tools ~$400 for the campaign window
Repeat: 30% of campaign buyers buy once more within 90 days at the same blended gross profit (~$8); confirm with company data
Velocity baseline unknown at store level; 10-K revenue decline suggests low single-digit units/store/week at many doors - measured week 0
Demo-day purchases (~20% of 3,600 sampled shoppers = ~720) are upside not counted in the funnel
DFW H-E-B stores carrying Braav biltong exist (locator lists H-E-B; third-party retail guides confirm H-E-B jerky-aisle placement); exact door count confirmed in week-0 shelf audit
Online offer: 4-bag starter pack at ~$35 with 20% off code BILTONG
Plan-B retail doors: if H-E-B declines sampling, shift demo shifts to Walmart/Sprouts TX stores carrying Braav (locator-verified)

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Thesis: Stryve does not need more doors - it needs shoppers who understand what biltong is and come back for it; It's Not Jerky turns H-E-B shelf space into repeat buyers [O1].
Problem: net sales fell 41% (10-K) while ~1,400 public reviews show only 4% discovered Braav in-store - distribution without velocity [S1][R3].
Opportunity: meat snacks +11.3% to $6.4B; biltong is the air-dried upgrade sitting in the same set [S6][R2].
Solution: DFW H-E-B demo days + shelf upgrade + taste-off creators, measured test-vs-control [O1][O2].
45-day goal: 2,000 attributed purchases and a velocity readout Stryve can take to buyers [O1].
slides.notes: Open with the paradox: the brand is on more shelves than ever while sales fell 41%. The problem is not distribution - it is what happens at the shelf.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Braav biltong: South African air-dried beef - cured and air-dried, never cooked like jerky; thick, tender, intensely beefy [S10].
Clean label: sugar-free, gluten-free, keto/paleo/whole30-friendly, 30g+ protein per serving; Original, Steak Bites, and Zero Sugar Hickory lines [S10][S4].
Retail ~$8-9 per 2.25oz bag (Sprouts $7.99, Walmart multipacks); Plano, TX HQ [S4][S1].
Sold DTC, on Amazon, and in H-E-B, Walmart, Whole Foods, Sprouts, CVS, Circle K and Love's [S2][S3].

visual.desc: Real Stryve Original pouch + bites product photography

slides.notes: The key sensory difference: jerky is cooked and shredded; biltong is air-dried whole muscle - denser, richer, chewier in a different way.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Stryve Foods Corp (NASDAQ: SNAX), Plano TX; founded by Ted Casey (Dymatize), ex-NFL player Gabe Carimi, and South African native Warren Pala [S1][S10].
Net sales $29.9M -> $17.7M (-41%) in FY2023; 10-K cites discontinuing 'non-profitable accounts' and rationalizing 'low-quality revenue' [S1].
Competitors in Texas biltong are fragmented regional players (Brooklyn Biltong, Shaka's, Billi Tong's, Lowfeld Soul Food); Stryve is the only national brand with H-E-B scale [S5].
Position: premium air-dried beef for performance and clean-label shoppers - the jerky upgrade, not another jerky [S10][R2].

Right: positioning map (x = commodity jerky to premium air-dried, y = mass-market to clean-label performance) with Jack Link's, Chomps, regional biltong brands, and Braav alone in the premium-clean quadrant

Baseline: week-0 shelf count via audit + company sell-through data [A3].
O2 (consideration): 3,600 in-store samples and 9,000 coupon claims [O2].
O3 (awareness): 1.5M Texas impressions and +12 points aided awareness of 'biltong' [O3].

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1 Performance Snackers, 18-34: DFW/Texas jerky buyers focused on macros; keto/paleo/whole30-curious; buy on protein and clean labels [S6][R2].
P2 Clean-Label H-E-B Parents, 30-50: weekly H-E-B shoppers wanting no-sugar, recognizable-ingredient snacks for lunchboxes [S6][S9].
Both share one need: a meat snack that is clearly better than jerky - the reason 12% of reviewers cite clean-label benefits and 5% compare it directly [R2].
Market: meat snacks +11.3% to $6.4B; high-protein snack positioning is the fastest-growing claim set in the aisle [S6][S8].

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary (complete): 10-K via last10k, company site/stores, Walmart/Sprouts listings, trade press - 10 sources [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5].

Primary, no-survey (complete): keyword-coded analysis of 1,400 public Stamped.io reviews [R1][R4] and a public distribution/digital-shelf audit of 8 sources [R5][R6] [S11][S12]; survey/interviews not run - published reviews skew positive.
Key results: sales -41% while doors multiplied [S1][R5]; taste and reorder dominate reviews [R1][R4]; only 4% discovered it in a store [R3]; biltong is an unfamiliar word in Texas [R6].
Influences: protein-snack boom (social), clean-label/keto trend (cultural), meat-snack growth +11.3% (market), retail app coupons (technological) [S6][S7][S9].
slides.notes: Name the methods and sample sizes out loud. The 10-K's 'low-quality revenue' line is the finding judges will remember.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: Finding: 1,400-review analysis - taste/flavor 29%, repeat/bulk 20%, only 4% found in store [R1][R3] -> in-store education, not more awareness ads.
Finding: SEC 10-K documents -41% sales and 'low-quality revenue' rationalization [S1] -> the campaign must produce sell-through proof, not impressions.
Finding: meat-snack category +11.3% while Stryve declines [S6] -> ride the tailwind with the air-dried upgrade positioning [R2].
Finding: reviews skew 5-star but 'found in store' is near-zero [R1][R3] -> demos + shelf talkers at the point of trial.
Finding: Texas HQ + DFW H-E-B doors [S2][S9] -> the test market is walkable and measurable.
slides.notes: Every decision traces to evidence. Point at the arrows, not the text.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Big idea: It's Not Jerky - biltong is air-dried, never cooked; a different product for a different shopper. Message: 'Love jerky? Try biltong.'
Positioning: for performance and clean-label shoppers who want more from a meat snack, Braav is the air-dried beef upgrade [S10][R2].

IMC mix, all testable: Paid geo-social -> store traffic; Earned Plano founder/ex-NFL story -> H-E-B buyer pitch; Shared #ItsNotJerky taste-off duets -> proof; Owned email/SMS + shelf talkers -> repeat [O1][O2].
Push-pull: H-E-B gets a measurable velocity test (push); shoppers get samples and a coupon (pull) [O1][O2].

Why: biltong is an unfamiliar word in Texas [R6] and only 4% of reviewers found it in a store [R3] - the shelf is where education must happen.
Measured: QR scans per store and units per store vs. control stores [O1].

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $15,000: social $5,500 [A4]; creators 3 x $1,000 [A6]; demos 12 x $250 [A7]; production $900 [A9]; tools $400 [A10]; contingency $2,200 [A11].
Funnel: 1.5M x 1.5% x 10% = 2,250 purchases at $18 avg = $40.5K [A1][A4].
The $2 coupon is manufacturer-funded, netted in revenue [A1][A8].
Conservative (50%): ROI ~-40%; ~720 demo purchases +$5.8K GP [A15] + repeat tail [A13] -> breakeven ~wk 10-12; plan-B doors if demos declined [A5][A18].
Margin sensitivity: at 35% GP (10-K low end) ROI ~-6%; breakeven margin ~37% - upside case holds at 45% [A2][S1].
slides.notes: Lead with honesty: conservative case loses in-window; the return comes from repeat buyers and from keeping shelf space the 10-K is rationalizing. Then show the test-vs-control design.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: attributed purchases; baseline 0; target 2,000; H-E-B coupon + Shopify code reports; weekly [O1].
O1: units per store per week, demo vs. control; baseline week-0 audit [A3]; target +25%; retailer data; weekly [O1].
O2: samples and claims; baseline 0; target 3,600 and 9,000; tally sheets + coupon platform; weekly [O2].
O3: 1.5M impressions; aided awareness of 'biltong' baseline at week 0 vs. post-campaign survey of 150 shoppers + non-campaign holdout DMAs; target +12 pts net of control [O3].
Trigger: under 30 QR scans per shift by week 3, move demos to top 3 stores; creator CTR under 1%, shift spend to Meta [A4].
slides.notes: Test vs. control is what a CPG buyer wants: proof the lift came from the campaign.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Thesis: Stryve does not need more doors - it needs shoppers who try it once to come back. It's Not Jerky turns H-E-B shelf space into repeat buyers [O1].
Projected: 2,000 purchases and $18.2K gross profit on $15K (21% ROI), plus a test-vs-control result Stryve can take to every retailer [A1][O1].
Mission: South African air-dried beef, made in Plano - kept on Texas shelves because Texans tried it [S1][S10].
Next: if test stores beat control by 25%, roll It's Not Jerky to more H-E-B stores and feed the velocity data the 10-K says is missing [O1][S1].
